title: Confianza
desc: Explaining a word to somebody who arrived last week
setting: Tom got here nine days ago, he has a notebook, and he has just asked you what confianza means.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: ¿Qué es eso de confianza? Yo lo entiendo como confiar, ¿verdad?
steps.en: What is this confianza thing? I take it as confiar, right?

options.es: Más o menos, pero no. Es un permiso que se gana con años.
options.en: More or less, but no. It is a permission you earn over years.
options.feedback: Confiar is what a bank does. Confianza is being able to walk in without knocking, and there is no word for that on the other side.

options.es: Sí, es más o menos eso.
options.en: Yes, it is more or less that.
options.feedback: It is not, and he will spend a year using it wrong because you did not want to complicate his ninth day.
True and useless. It cannot be translated, so explain it in Spanish, which is what you now know how to do.

options.es: Para entrar sin tocar. Para agarrar un vaso sin pedirlo.
options.en: To walk in without knocking. To take a glass without asking for it.
options.feedback: Two concrete pictures beat any definition. That is how you explain a word inside the language instead of around it.

options.es: Para tratar a alguien sin tanto cuidado.
options.en: To deal with somebody less carefully.
options.feedback: Accurate and abstract. Nine days in, he needs the door and the glass.

options.es: Ya lo vas a ir sintiendo.
options.en: You will get a feel for it.
options.feedback: He will, in about two years. He asked now and you have the answer now.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.es: ¿Y cómo sé si alguien me tiene confianza?
steps.en: And how do I know if somebody has confianza with me?

options.es: Cuando te empiecen a corregir. A la visita no se le corrige.
options.en: When they start correcting you. You do not correct a guest.
options.feedback: That is the test and somebody had to tell you it too. Being corrected is the promotion, and until then everything you do wrong is politely absorbed.

options.es: Cuando te inviten a comer sin avisar.
options.en: When they feed you without warning you.
options.feedback: A good sign and it happens on day one, to everybody. The correction is the one that only happens later.

options.es: Cuando te digan que sí a todo.
options.en: When they say yes to everything.
options.feedback: That is the opposite. Yes to everything is what people say to somebody they are still being careful with.

steps.speaker: Tom
steps.en: Ideay. I am going to write that down.

options.es: Apuntalo, sí. Yo tenía un cuaderno igual.
options.en: Write it down, yes. I had a notebook just like that.
options.feedback: You had one, you filled it, and somebody stood on a corner explaining words to you. This is the same afternoon from the other side.
Fine. Telling him you had the same notebook is worth more to him than the definition was.

options.en: There is no need to write that down.
options.feedback: There is. It took you three years to work out and he can have it on his ninth day.
